title: Late Set At The Blue Room
subject: the last set of the night at a jazz club
caption: Jazz fusion with a big band. Full brass section with tight stabs and a shout chorus, Rhodes electric piano comping extended chords, upright bass walking, drums riding on the hi-hat with brushes switching to sticks. A soulful male baritone sings the head, scats through the solo section and runs melismas on the way out. Warm analog saturation, plate reverb, the room audible behind the horns. 112 BPM, B-flat major. Warm, loose, after-hours.
lyrics:
[Intro - Brass]

[Verse 1]
The kitchen closed an hour ago
The waiters are doing the sums
Eleven people and a bartender
And the band plays like it's a thousand

[Pre-Chorus]
This is the set we actually came for

[Chorus]
Late set at the Blue Room
Nobody's watching the clock
The drummer's smiling at something
That happened four bars ago

[Scat Solo]
Doo-ba-dee, ba-doo-dat
Sha-ba-doo-wah

[Verse 2]
The trumpet player's wife came down
She sits where she always sits
He plays the ballad slightly differently
And everybody notices

[Brass Solo]

[Chorus]
Late set at the Blue Room
Nobody's watching the clock
The drummer's smiling at something
That happened four bars ago

[Outro - Scat]
Ba-doo-dat, doo-ba-dee
